review_role: Chief Medical Officer agent; evidence review, not human clinician signoff

choice.reason: This value is inside a real adult assay reference below 5 mg/L while clearly above the European persistent-risk modifier above 2 mg/L. The larger visual separation teaches the overlap better than 2.1 mg/L.
choice.dataset_boundary: This is an independent labelled teaching example. Do not change Alex's fictional 2.1 mg/L result, history or context elsewhere.

graphic.overlap_meaning: Above the persistent-risk modifier yet inside this example laboratory reference. It is a reason to review context, not a diagnosis or a band of inevitable disease.
graphic.below_threshold_meaning: Below this particular modifier threshold; not a guarantee of low overall risk or optimal longevity.
avoid: A risk-probability y-axis or invented future-risk curve
A single high result establishes persistent inflammation
A universal hs-CRP treatment target or automatic drug recommendation
graphic.status: Historical proposed graph parameters; superseded by the comparison-based version 64 candidate.

medical_meaning.lab: Within this illustrative assay reference, not proof of optimal health.
medical_meaning.prevention: Persistently elevated hs-CRP above 2 mg/L is a cardiovascular risk modifier in the 2025 ESC/EAS framework, considered with overall risk and particularly around treatment-decision thresholds.
medical_meaning.future_health: Higher CRP is associated with later cardiovascular events in prospective evidence. This sample does not predict whether or when one person will develop disease.
medical_meaning.repeat: Confirm persistence when clinically stable; avoid drawing cardiovascular conclusions during acute illness or active infection and consider injury/other inflammatory causes.
medical_meaning.interval: No universal repeat interval should be imposed by this landing example. Clinical context determines timing.
medical_meaning.longevity_term: Prefer prevention threshold, risk-review threshold, or evidence-based thresholds for long-term health. No independently validated universal longevity-optimal interval is being defined here.

en.takeaway: Within range. Still worth a closer look.
en.qualifier: Repeat when well. Lab limits vary. Not a diagnosis.

es.prevention_verdict: Valorar con tu contexto de salud.
es.takeaway: Dentro del intervalo. Aun así, merece otra mirada.
es.qualifier: Repetir cuando estés bien. Los límites varían entre laboratorios. No es un diagnóstico.

approved_closed_copy_direction.copy_note: These medically approved directions can be shortened by the copy specialist provided persistence, wider context, laboratory variation and the no-diagnosis meaning remain clear. The long-term perspective label must not be rendered as a universal numerical optimum.

sources.role: Actual assay reference and clinical interpretation context
sources.title: CDC NHANES 2021–2023 hs-CRP laboratory procedure manual, Roche Cobas 8000
sources.location: Section 13, PDF page 18 (zero-based page 17), lines 643–645 in web extraction; clinical relevance section PDF page 3.
sources.interpretation: A documented Roche adult reference, used here illustratively. The manual also states that increases are nonspecific and require a complete medical history.

sources.role: European risk modifier applicable to Spain
sources.title: 2025 Focused Update of the 2019 ESC/EAS Guidelines for the management of dyslipidaemias
sources.location: Box 1, risk modifiers beyond SCORE2/SCORE2-OP; in the co-published Atherosclerosis PDF this is PDF page 6. Official ESC slide set also reproduces the risk-modifier box.
sources.interpretation: A modifier of overall cardiovascular risk, not a universal diagnosis, optimal interval or automatic treatment threshold.
sources.verification: Primary article indexed text, official ESC slide excerpt and the co-published primary guideline PDF were checked. Local primary PDF text retained for table verification.

sources.role: Large prospective evidence for association with later events
sources.title: C-reactive protein concentration and risk of coronary heart disease, stroke, and mortality: individual participant meta-analysis
sources.study: Emerging Risk Factors Collaboration, Lancet 2010; 160,309 people without prior vascular disease from 54 prospective studies.
sources.interpretation: Higher CRP was associated with later coronary disease and ischaemic stroke after adjustment. Do not convert the study's relative associations into a personalized risk percentage for this sample.

sources.title: American Heart Association hsCRP Toolkit for Professionals
sources.location: PDF page 1 practical advice, and page 2 decision-making note.
sources.interpretation: Measure when clinically stable, avoid acute illness/active infection, confirm elevated results and assess other causes. The US ≥2 threshold differs at the exact boundary from the European >2 wording chosen for this graphic.

sources.title: American Heart Association: An hsCRP test can add clarity to your heart health picture
sources.interpretation: Describes hsCRP as an inflammation marker linked with heart-attack/stroke risk, and repeated elevations prompting evaluation of other inflammatory causes and discussion of next steps.

sources.title: Association between C reactive protein and coronary heart disease: Mendelian randomisation analysis
sources.interpretation: Genetic evidence does not support circulating CRP itself as a causal determinant of coronary heart disease. It remains useful as a risk marker in clinical context.

alternatives_considered.decision: Not selected for this particular comparison
alternatives_considered.reason: LDL has strong causal atherosclerosis evidence, but its prevention/treatment goals depend on overall cardiovascular risk. A generic normal-vs-longevity-optimal graphic would conflate a lab's reporting cut-off with an individualized target. It is a good later example if risk category and treatment context are supplied explicitly.

Different diagnostic thresholds may help teach context, but are less directly aligned with the named starter panel; no implication should be made that HbA1c or fasting glucose is included in this kit.

source_quote_policy: Only short source excerpts are quoted. This is an agent evidence review, not proof that a human CMO has clinically approved the public site.

current_approved_representation.type: Two explicit inequalities, with no ruler or axis.
current_approved_representation.lab: 3.2 < 5 mg/L: below the example lab reference limit.
current_approved_representation.prevention: 3.2 > 2 mg/L if persistent: above the review modifier.
current_approved_representation.historical_domain_note: The former 0–6 domain and percentage positions were graphical choices, not clinical requirements.
